records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Introduction to Anthropology
records.description: Explores what it means to be human through biological anthropology (human evolution), archaeology (material remains of past peoples), sociocultural anthropology (present peoples), and linguistics (language).

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Global Discoveries in Archaeology
records.description: Impact of well-known archaeological sites on our understanding of the past.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Mythbusting in Archaeology
records.description: A critical exploration of pseudo-scientific claims and fantastical interpretations of archaeological sites and objects in popular media.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Art and Society
records.description: Art as an expression of social and cultural systems in non-Western societies.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Global Cultural Diversity
records.description: Introduction to the field of cultural anthropology; examination of how cultures vary and are similar.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Health, Healing, and Medicine Across Cultures
records.description: Anthropological perspective on health, disease, and medical/curing systems; relationships between culture, biology, political-economic environments, disease, and curing examined. Recommended preparation: ANTH 101 or 203.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Health Divides: Human Inequality and Well-Being
records.description: A critical exploration of how systemic inequalities along lines of class, race, gender, and sexuality become embodied in adverse health outcomes.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Material Culture of Confinement and Incarceration
records.description: The impact of confinement and incarceration on human lives across both time and space.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Perspectives on Race and Human Variation
records.description: Critical examination of the history of racial classification and social hierarchy, influences of biology and culture on human variation, and differences among groups.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Archaeological Methods and Interpretation
records.description: Archaeological methods with a focus on how we use data to reconstruct past human lifeways.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: The Pyramids of Egypt: Why and How?
records.description: Archaeology of the social, political, economic, and technological developments that are indicated by the pyramids of ancient Egypt.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Introduction to the Study of Language
records.description: Introduction to the ways in which sound, meaning, and structure of words and sentences in natural languages are described and analyzed by linguists. (Crosslisted course offered as ENGLISH 256, ANTH 256.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
records.description: Evidence for human evolution; evolutionary explanations of human and primate variation; techniques of biological anthropology.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Sex, Evolution, and Human Nature
records.description:
Human sexuality, relations across sexes and genders, parenting, cooperation, and violence compared across cultures and to nonhuman primates, using evolutionary and
biocultural perspectives.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Skeleton Keys: The Basics of Forensic Anthropology
records.description: Examination of forensic anthropology techniques to identify human skeletal remains in a medicolegal context.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Field Methods
records.description: Practice in methods of archaeological, ethnological, or linguistic field research.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Arts and Media in Global Perspective
records.description: Contemporary arts and media around the world, and their impact on identity, society, and culture.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Childhood and Culture
records.description: Anthropological theory and methods applied to the study of infant, child, and adolescent development.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: The Anthropology of Religious Experience
records.description: Body, meaning, and power in religion cross culturally.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Cross-Cultural Perspectives of Mental Health and Illness
records.description: Cross-cultural mental health and illness; common U.S. mental illnesses and treatments in diverse cultures around the world; mental illnesses specific to particular cultures. Recommended preparation: PSYCH 105; ANTH 101 or 203.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Anthropology of Epidemic Disease and Bioterrorism
records.description: Cross-cultural understanding of how humans respond to epidemics, including high mortality diseases, diseases common in the developing world, and diseases that pose future threats.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Contemporary Cultures and Peoples of Africa
records.description: Introduction to family, social, political, economic and religious institutions of African cultures in context of African social issues.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Cultural Ecology
records.description: Ecological/environmental anthropology relevant to questions of population, resources, cognition, health and livelihoods.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Contemporary Human Issues
records.description: Journey into numerous and dynamic contemporary human issues in American society focusing on their interconnectivity with equity, justice, and social power.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Gender in Cross Cultural Perspective
records.description: Cross-cultural examination of gendered status and roles, sexuality and marriage, folk concepts of sexual anatomy in Western and non-Western societies; concepts of nature and culture are explored through a variety of perspectives. Recommended preparation: Sophomore standing. (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 316, WGSS 316.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Global Feminisms
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ANTH 101, WGSS 101, or WGSS 120.
records.description: An interdisciplinary approach to examining women's roles and experiences throughout the world and different approaches to feminism/feminisms. (Crosslisted course offered as WGSS 332, ANTH 317.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Native Peoples of North America
records.description: A holistic exploration of various Indigenous peoples and cultures of North America, through the lens of anthropology. (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 320, AIS 320.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Indigenous Women: Activism and Agency
records.description: An in-depth examination of Indigenous women's roles in their societies both traditionally and in the contemporary world.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Contemporary Native Peoples of the Americas
records.description: Contemporary cultures of Native American communities emphasizing North America. (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 327, AIS 327.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Origins of Culture and Civilization
records.description: Origins of human culture from the beginnings of humankind to the rise of the first civilizations in Africa and Eurasia. Recommended preparation: 3 hours ANTH.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Archaeology of the Americas
records.description: Archaeological investigations of cultures and environments of the Americas.  (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 331, AIS 331.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Time and Culture in the Northwest
records.description: The archaeologically reconstructed environmental and cultural past of the Northwest including contemporary scientific and social approaches and issues. Recommended preparation: ANTH 101.  (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 334, AIS 334.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: States and Empires in Africa and Eurasia
records.description: Overview of past urbanism, states and empires in the eastern hemisphere; survey of European, African and Asian archaeology.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Maya, Aztec and Inca Civilizations
records.description: Examination of the archaeology of Mesoamerica and South America. Recommended preparation: 3 credits ANTH.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Speech, Thought, and Culture
records.description: The role of language in social situations and as a reflection of cultural differences.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Historical Linguistics
records.description: Origins and evolution of human language, relationships between peoples and languages, development of contemporary ethnicities, linguistical change, reconstructive methods, and writing systems.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Darwinian Medicine
records.description: Overview of Darwinian medicine; theoretical foundations, insights, and key research contributions and applications from this interdisciplinary field.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: The Archaeology of Climate Change
records.description: Exploration of the connections between climate change and people from the Ice Age to the present.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Human Osteology
records.description: Introduction to the field of osteology including molecular analysis, paleopathology, taphonomy and forensic analysis.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
records.description: Evolution of primate behavior from ecological and phylogenetic perspective emphasizing methods for understanding primate adaptations and diversity. Recommended preparation: ANTH 101 or BIOLOGY 101, 102 or 150.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: History of Anthropological Thought
records.description: Development of theories in anthropology including contributions of significant individuals, representative classics and influential current movements.  Recommended preparation:  Junior standing.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Topics in Anthropology
records.description: Examination of selected topics in contemporary anthropological theory and practice.  Recommended preparation: Junior standing.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Archaeological Field School
records.description: Training in methods of archaeological data recovery and analysis.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: The Self in Culture
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: One course at the 100-level and one course at the 200-level in any of the following subjects: AMER ST, ANTH, ART, CES, COM, ENGLISH, H D, HISTORY, HUMANITY, PHIL, POL S, PSYCH, SOC, or WGSS; junior standing.
records.description: Survey of anthropological theories exploring self in Western/non-Western cultures through dreams, history, and human development.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Medical Anthropology
records.description: Relationships among disease, curing, culture and environment; non-Western medical systems; political economy of health care. Recommended preparation: Junior standing.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: History of American Indian Sovereignty and Federal Indian Law
records.description: The history of sovereignty and Federal Indian Law against the backdrop of treaties and trust responsibility. (Crosslisted course offered as HISTORY 410, ANTH 410, POL S 410.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Anthropology and World Problems
records.description: Data and methods of cultural anthropology applied to the solution of contemporary human problems, emphasizing sustainable development. Recommended preparation: 3 hours ANTH; junior standing.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Human Issues in International Development
records.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of complex interaction in the context of colonial and post-colonial development.  (Crosslisted course offered as ANTH 418, POL S 418, SOC 418.)

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Archaeological Theory and Explanation
records.description: Archaeological theory and the role of theories of culture change in crafting explanations for the human past. Recommended preparation: ANTH 230; ANTH 330 or 331.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Ethnolinguistics
records.description: Anthropological theory and methods applied to the study of cognitive linguistics, or the interrelation of language, mind, and culture. Credit not granted for more than one of ANTH 450 and ANTH 550.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Museum Anthropology
records.description: Exploration of anthropology museums within the broader museum field and the history of field anthropology, including hands-on experience with museum work. Credit not granted for both ANTH 455 and ANTH 555.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Introduction to Anthropological Demography and Epidemiology
records.description: Small-scale population dynamics; culture change; event history analysis; evolutionary life history; risk; reproduction; morbidity; and mortality in ethnographic, historical, and archaeological populations. Recommended preparation: ANTH 260. Credit not granted for both ANTH 463 and ANTH 563.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Hormones and Human Reproduction
records.description: Hormones, diet, and stress in the regulation of human reproduction, behavior, and physiology; menstruation, parenting, and pregnancy; evolution of reproduction. Recommended preparation: ANTH 260, BIOLOGY 107, 150, or equivalent.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Human Evolution
records.description: Human origins in the light of the fossil record and evolutionary theory. Credit not granted for both ANTH 465 and ANTH 565. Recommended preparation: ANTH 260.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Evolution of Cooperation
records.description: Human cooperation from an evolutionary perspective, as informed by research from anthropology, biology, ecology, economics, and psychology; discussion-based seminar.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Genes, Culture and Human Diversity
records.description: Relationships between genes, language and culture are explored as a means to understanding world history, genetic and cultural diversity and unity. Recommended preparation: Junior standing.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Evolution and Society
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ANTH 260 or BIOLOGY 301; junior standing.
records.description: Survey of how the theory of evolution is used to better understand ourselves, the societies in which live, and the biological world on which we depend. Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 305, 395, 403, or 405 or concurrent enrollment. (Crosslisted course offered as BIOLOGY 473, ANTH 473.)
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Integrative Themes in Anthropology
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ANTH 203; ANTH 230; ANTH 260; ANTH 390; junior standing (senior standing strongly recommended).
records.description: Current research crosscutting traditional subdisciplines of anthropology.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Research Practicum
records.description: Hands-on experience in selection of a research problem, review of literature, developing methodology, data collection, and reporting results.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Anthropology Internship
records.description: Participation as archaeological or cultural anthropological intern in public or private sectors; requires special arrangement with faculty advisor.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ANTH
records.title: Special Problems
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
